clue.text: Actor, do this and you'll fail the audition?

definitions.meaning: a performer who learns a lead's role in order to stand in

definitions.text: do this and you'll fail the audition?
definitions.meaning: split in two, the word reads as studying too little, which would sink an audition

explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in performer who learns a lead's role is called this; split in two, the word also suggests too little preparation.

clue.text: Capable of leading the Open — initially!

parts.note: a player leading a contest is up, ahead of the field

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A golfer good enough to head the leaderboard at the Open, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'the' and 'Open', giving TO; the Open is a famous golf championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Being equal to a task, as in 'not feeling well enough for it', is the idiom meant.

clue.text: Calls for reform of prison after start of debate

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters follow that single letter
start of picks the opening letter of the word debate
reform of asks for the letters of prison to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone demands prison reform once a debate gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calls' looks like a noun, but it is the verb sense of visiting briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: To visit casually, as in 'pays a call', is a phrasal-verb synonym for calls.

clue.text: Foie gras paste is served in process of initiation

indicators.note: food that is served is dished up and arranged, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gourmet pâté is part of some formal induction ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is served' rearranges all thirteen letters of FOIE GRAS PASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremony or event marking someone's entry into a new stage of life or group is this ritual.

clue.text: Choke or accelerator

definitions.meaning: to strangle someone by the neck
the valve or pedal controlling an engine's fuel flow and so its speed

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to strangle and the engine control that regulates fuel and speed.

clue.text: Name given to opera singer's place of rest

indicators.note: given to says the abbreviation is added on to the singer

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female opera singer

explanation.surface: A soprano's name is bestowed on her final resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: A low backless couch or bed is somewhere to lie down and rest.

clue.text: Tucked up with a graduate teacher

parts.note: BEd, Bachelor of Education, is the degree held by a graduate teacher

explanation.surface: Someone lies in bed beside a newly qualified schoolteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: BEd is the British teaching degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in bed is an old-fashioned adverb for lying tucked up for the night.

clue.text: A non-conformist, Clegg is rumoured to support defeat

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: to defeat is to beat

indicators.note: a rumour is passed by word of mouth, so the name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Nick Clegg was a British Liberal Democrat leader and deputy prime minister

explanation.surface: A rebel politician, Clegg, is said to be propping up a losing cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg was the UK's deputy prime minister 2010-15.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the 1950s Beat Generation who rejected conventional society is a classic rebel figure.

clue.text: Party entitled to change sign here

parts.note: a do is a party or social function

indicators.note: to change asks for the letters of entitled to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A guest list where those entitled may change what is printed.
explanation.definitionFit: On a form, a row of dots marks the spot where a signature belongs.

clue.text: Rat attached to end of cat's foot

indicators.note: attached to says the scoundrel is joined on after the single letter
end of picks the final letter of the word cat's

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person, a rotter

explanation.surface: A rat clinging to the tail of a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's foot, especially as food, is called by this name.

clue.text: Tramp proclaimed ill-defined harangue

indicators.note: proclaimed means spoken out, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a vague rant is an ill-defined harangue

explanation.surface: A rough sleeper shouts a rambling tirade at passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: A homeless wanderer with no settled home is a synonym for a tramp.

clue.text: Sit in carriage, being moved to see doctors

indicators.note: letters being moved around are rearranged

explanation.surface: Patients are told to sit in a carriage to be taken to their doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being moved' rearranges all thirteen letters of SIT IN CARRIAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicians who specialise in the care of elderly people are a kind of doctor.

clue.text: Popular farmhouse on film becomes target area

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed on means written after

parts.note: to film a scene is to shoot it
something popular is in, fashionable
a grange is a country house with farm buildings

explanation.surface: A trendy farmhouse in a film is turned into a firing area.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where people practise firing guns at targets.

clue.text: Outside study, student ties up long hair

indicators.note: outside says the mooring word wraps around the other two pieces

parts.note: a boat docks when it ties up at a quay
to read a subject is to study it at university
L, for learner, is the usual abbreviation for a student

explanation.surface: A student outside the study fastens up their long hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Long matted ropes of hair, as worn by many Rastafarians.

clue.text: Draw on evidence of engagement as opener

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed on means written after

parts.note: an engagement ring shows a couple are betrothed
to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: A fiancée shows off her engagement ring as an ice-breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The tab on a drinks can that you tug to open it.

clue.text: Device for lifting a large beast

parts.note: a jack is used for raising a car
L is the usual abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A tool for raising a very big animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild dog of Africa and Asia is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Exposed well-dressed fool

parts.note: a secret that is out has been exposed
smart means well-dressed

explanation.surface: A dapper idiot is unmasked.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the better of someone by cunning is to trick or fool them.

clue.text: Nick a car and set off

parts.note: RR, Rolls-Royce, is a crossword standard for a car

indicators.note: off indicates the letters of set are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Steal a vehicle and drive away.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to nick a criminal is to seize them for the police.

clue.text: Engineers cutting short visit about IT performance

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps

indicators.note: about says the shortened word goes round the two letters
cutting short removes the final letter of the word for visit

parts.note: to pay a call is to visit

explanation.surface: Army engineers cut a visit short over a computer problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting short' turns CALL into CAL, which goes 'about' IT to make CITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A concert given by a soloist or small group is a type of performance.

clue.text: Person responsible for issue of paper?

definitions.text: Person responsible for issue of paper?

parts.words: Person responsible for issue of paper?
parts.note: issue means offspring, so the person looking after a child; it also names a British daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Who is in charge of putting out a newspaper edition?
explanation.definitionFit: A legal carer of a child shares a name with a national British newspaper.

clue.text: Disease requiring peace and quiet? No way

indicators.note: No here says the abbreviation for a road must be dropped

parts.note: calm silence is a state of being motionless and still
St, street, is a kind of way

explanation.surface: An ailment that demands rest and silence, without exception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way' looks like an exclamation of refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sickness or ailment is a direct synonym of disease.

clue.text: Want one state to adopt a platform, being ineffectual

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the platform goes inside

parts.note: to want something is to lack it
I is the Roman numeral one
Cal is an abbreviation for California
a dais is a raised platform

explanation.surface: A demand for a state to adopt a manifesto leaves it weak.
explanation.walkthrough: Cal is a standard abbreviation for California; 'to adopt' puts the platform inside the run of pieces, just after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking enthusiasm or energy describes someone listless and weak in action.

clue.text: Sloane Ranger backing shows venue

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
shows means the letters are on display inside the words Sloane Ranger

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A posh Sloane Ranger lends financial support to a stage venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'shows venue' as the definition, but 'shows' is the sign that letters sit inside the words. A Sloane Ranger is a stereotypical upper-class young Londoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium or hall where events and spectacles are staged is a kind of venue.

clue.text: Naked and poor — that covers the start of life

indicators.note: that covers says the word for poor wraps around the letter

parts.note: poor quality means bad

indicators.note: the start of picks the first letter of life

explanation.surface: Born nude and penniless at life's beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare and lacking covering, as a bald tyre or bald statement is plain and naked.

clue.text: Tom might have one for the road!

definitions.text: Tom might have one for the road!

parts.words: Tom might have one for the road!
parts.note: a tom is a male cat, which has eyes; also a reflecting stud set into roads

explanation.surface: A friend called Tom stops for a final drink before leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflective stud marking traffic lanes takes its name from a feline's glowing eyes.

clue.text: A meal out with daughter, and a walk through the trees

indicators.note: out signals the letters of A meal are put out of order

explanation.surface: A family lunch outdoors, followed by a woodland stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree-lined public promenade, a Spanish word used in English.

clue.text: Deposit one left in road

indicators.note: in says the two letters go inside the road

parts.note: St, street, is a road
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a single item in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine sediment left behind by a river is a kind of deposit.

clue.text: Imagined volunteers changing sides, following supporter

indicators.note: following says the next pieces come after the supporter

parts.note: a fan supports a team
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: changing asks for the letters of sides to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Army volunteers who defect after backing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To daydream or picture something in the mind is a synonym for imagined.
